events.text: Objective: Determine whether there is sufficient public evidence to justify Hellberg Safety investing in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case beyond its current hearing-protection offering.. Constraints: Limited to publicly available information; no internal company data.; Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeline for any proposed experiment.; Must identify evidence of consumer demand, willingness to pay, and competitive positioning.; Must consider existing B2B relationships and current reach to individual buyers.. Alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition targeting a specific use case (e.g., outdoor recreation, construction, medical).; 2) Expand the existing hearing-protection line into adjacent consumer segments without differentiation (e.g., standard earplugs for general use).; 3) No expansion: continue focusing on existing B2B hearing and face protection markets.; 4) Change route to market or customer group (e.g., sell directly to consumers online, partner with retailers, target a new demographic).; 5) Redesign existing products for a new use case (e.g., add comfort features for extended wear)..

T1: Consumers will adopt a differentiated consumer proposition if they perceive the product as a lifestyle accessory that enhances enjoyment of specific activities (e.g., outdoor recreation, music, sports). Who benefits: Consumers seeking comfort and style for activities they already engage in.. Why behaviour changes: Shifting from functional necessity to a lifestyle choice increases willingness to purchase multiple units and pay a premium for design and comfort.. How value is captured: Hellberg can capture value through premium pricing, direct-to-consumer sales, and brand extension that differentiates from industrial protection.. Assumptions: Consumers currently view hearing protection as purely functional.; There is a growing market segment willing to invest in lifestyle-oriented earplugs.; Hellberg can design and market a product that meets aesthetic and comfort expectations without compromising protection.. Predictions: In a test offering a differentiated consumer product, purchase intent will be higher than for a standard industrial earplug.; Surveyed consumers will cite enjoyment of activities as the primary reason for purchase.; Willingness to pay will be at least 20% above the price of a standard industrial earplug..

T2: Consumers will adopt a differentiated consumer proposition if they perceive the product as a safety requirement for specific activities (e.g., construction, medical, industrial) where compliance is mandatory. Who benefits: Professional users and employers who must meet regulatory standards for hearing protection.. Why behaviour changes: Mandatory compliance reduces purchase friction and increases willingness to pay for certified, compliant products.. How value is captured: Hellberg can capture value through premium pricing justified by certification, B2B contracts, and partnerships with safety regulators.. Assumptions: Regulatory bodies require specific hearing protection standards for certain activities.; Professional users currently purchase earplugs through industrial suppliers rather than directly.; Compliance is a primary purchase driver for these users.. Predictions: In a test offering a differentiated product, purchase intent will be higher among users who cite compliance requirements.; Willingness to pay will be at least 15% above the price of a standard industrial earplug.; Sales will be concentrated in B2B channels rather than direct-to-consumer..

Test "Consumer Proposition Preference Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with simulated product offers and willingness-to-pay questions.. Sample: 500 respondents: 250 self-identified outdoor/recreation enthusiasts and 250 self-identified professional/industrial users.. Measure: 1) Purchase intent (binary: would buy). 2) Primary reason for purchase (open-ended). 3) Maximum price willing to pay (EUR).. Predictions: T1: Enthusiast group will show higher purchase intent and cite enjoyment of activities as primary reason, with willingness to pay at least 20% above standard industrial earplug price.; T2: Professional group will show higher purchase intent and cite compliance requirements as primary reason, with willingness to pay at least 15% above standard industrial earplug price.. Decision rule: If enthusiast group purchase intent >= 40% and compliance reason < 20% of responses, proceed to develop a lifestyle proposition. If professional group purchase intent >= 40% and compliance reason < 20% of responses, proceed to develop a compliance proposition. If neither condition is met, do not expand.. Cost: 18000 euros, 10 weeks.

Favours T1: Do not invest in a differentiated consumer proposition at this time. Public evidence does not demonstrate consumer demand for a lifestyle-oriented product, nor does it address willingness to pay a premium for design and comfort. The existing B2B relationships and current reach to individual buyers suggest a need for further validation before committing resources. Beliefs: T1: uncertain; T2: unlikely.

T1 kept: Simulated evidence SYN-D concerns a warehouse label printer and packing errors, which does not address consumer perception of earplugs as lifestyle accessories or willingness to pay a premium for design and comfort. Therefore it does not affect T1. New claim: none. Evidence: SYN-D.

Recommendation: Do not invest in a differentiated consumer proposition at this time. Public evidence does not demonstrate consumer demand for a lifestyle-oriented product, nor does it address willingness to pay a premium for design and comfort. The existing B2B relationships and current reach to individual buyers suggest a need for further validation before committing resources. Target customer: Professional/industrial users who must meet regulatory compliance for hearing protection.. Value proposition: Premium, certified hearing protection products that meet specific activity requirements, leveraging Hellberg’s existing safety reputation and compliance capabilities.. Favoured theory: T2. Next action: Conduct the proposed Consumer Proposition Preference Test (or a smaller validation study) to measure purchase intent and willingness to pay among professional users. If results meet the decision thresholds, proceed to develop a compliance‑f. Uncertainty: The evidence base is limited to company claims and a single simulated result; no independent consumer survey or market data was read. The test budget and timeline may also constrain validation.. Would change if: A validated consumer survey shows purchase intent above 40% and willingness to pay at least 15% above standard industrial earplug price, indicating strong demand for a lifestyle proposition.; Independent market data reveals a growing consumer market for hearing protection products, particularly among outdoor and music enthusiasts, with measurable willingness to pay a premium.. Beliefs: T1: uncertain; T2: unlikely.

T1: Homeowners will purchase a differentiated consumer lawn tractor because it becomes an affordable, convenient chore solution for small gardens and outdoor tasks, and Deere can capture value through premium pricing and brand differentiation. Who benefits: Individual homeowners with small gardens who previously lacked efficient outdoor equipment.. Why behaviour changes: Increased awareness of the convenience and practicality of garden tractors, combined with the desire for easier outdoor maintenance, makes ownership seem like a sensible purchase.. How value is captured: Deere can charge a premium price for a purpose-built consumer model, sell through independent dealers, and maintain brand prestige while capturing higher margins than standard farm equipment.. Assumptions: Homeowners perceive garden tractors as a legitimate chore tool rather than a farm necessity.; Independent dealers will stock and service the consumer model effectively.; Marketing can communicate the value proposition to potential buyers.. Predictions: A survey of homeowners will show a higher intent to purchase a consumer lawn tractor than a generic farm tractor.; Sales of the intended consumer model will exceed the sales of a comparable generic model in the same market.; Deere's consumer segment will generate higher profit margins than its farm segment..

T2: Small‑farm owners will adopt a differentiated consumer lawn tractor because it reduces labor costs and improves efficiency for light‑to‑moderate farming tasks, and Deere can capture value through volume sales and service contracts. Who benefits: Small‑farm owners with limited labor and budget who need efficient equipment for light‑to‑moderate tasks.. Why behaviour changes: Economic pressure to lower labor costs and the need for efficient equipment for light‑to‑moderate farming tasks makes a consumer‑grade lawn tractor seem like a cost‑effective investment.. How value is captured: Deere can sell through independent dealers, offer service and parts contracts, and capture volume sales while maintaining a premium price for a purpose‑built model.. Assumptions: Small‑farm owners are willing to invest in equipment that reduces labor costs.; Independent dealers can provide the necessary service and parts for a consumer model.; The market size for small‑farm owners is sufficient to justify production.. Predictions: A survey of small‑farm owners will show higher intent to purchase a consumer lawn tractor than a generic farm tractor.; Sales of the intended consumer model will exceed the sales of a comparable generic model among small‑farm owners.; Deere's consumer segment will generate higher revenue per unit than its farm segment..

Test "Consumer vs. Small-Farm Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging. Recruit 400 respondents: 200 homeowners with small gardens and 200 small-farm owners. Randomly assign participants to one of two message groups: Homeowner group receives a chore-focused proposition (e.g., 'Easily maintain your small garden with a Deere lawn tractor—save time and effort!'); Small-farm group receives a farming-focused proposition (e.g., 'Increase efficiency and reduce labor costs with a Deere small-farm lawn tractor'). Both groups view a product description of the same intended consumer model (e.g., a 1962-style Deere lawn tractor). Measure purchase intent (binary: would buy) and willingness to pay (WTP) on a 1‑10 scale.. Sample: 400 respondents (200 homeowners, 200 small-farm owners) recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and geographic region.. Measure: Purchase intent (binary: would buy) and willingness to pay (WTP) on a 1‑10 scale.. Predictions: T1: Homeowners will show higher purchase intent and WTP than small-farm owners, indicating demand for a chore-focused proposition.; T2: Small-farm owners will show higher purchase intent and WTP than homeowners, indicating demand for a farming-focused proposition.. Decision rule: If the average purchase intent of the Homeowner group is at least 10 points higher than that of the Small-farm group, conclude T1 is supported. If the average purchase intent of the Small-farm group is at least 10 points higher than that of the Homeowner group, conclude T2 is supported. If the difference is less than 10 points, both theories remain plausible and further testing is needed.. Cost: 8000 euros, 6 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition for homeowners with small gardens, leveraging the existing tractor engineering and independent dealer network. The evidence shows a 76% rise in lawn and garden equipment sales and the success of the 4010 model, which supports the idea that homeowners are willing to purchase a consumer lawn tractor for chore purposes. A targeted test could further validate demand and WTP Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

New claim: Homeowners will purchase a differentiated consumer lawn tractor because it becomes an affordable, convenient chore solution for small gardens and outdoor tasks, and Deere can capture value through premium pricing and brand differentiation.. Recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition for homeowners with small gardens, leveraging the existing tractor engineering and independent dealer network. The evidence shows a 76% rise in lawn and garden equipment sales and the success of the 4010 model, which supports the idea that homeowners are willing to purchase a consumer lawn tractor for chore purposes. A targeted test could further validate demand and WTP Target customer: Homeowners with small gardens who currently lack efficient outdoor equipment for chore tasks.. Value proposition: A purpose-built consumer lawn tractor that offers convenience, ease of use, and brand reliability, sold through independent dealers at a premium price.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed Consumer vs. Small-Farm Messaging Test (400 respondents, 6 weeks, €8,000) to measure purchase intent and willingness to pay for chore versus farming-focused messaging.. Uncertainty: The size of the homeowner market and their willingness to pay a premium for a consumer lawn tractor remain uncertain. The test will clarify whether homeowners are the primary target.. Would change if: If the test shows small-farm owners expressing higher purchase intent and willingness to pay than homeowners, the recommendation would shift to a farming-focused proposition.; If the test shows no significant difference in purchase intent between homeowners and small-farm owners, both theories would remain plausible and further market research would be needed.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Test "Differentiated vs Standard Earplug Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized product exposure. Participants are randomly assigned to view either a differentiated product for a specific use case (e.g., outdoor recreation) or a standard earplug. Predictions: T1: Higher purchase intent and WTP for the differentiated product than for the standard earplug.; T2: No significant difference in purchase intent and WTP between the differentiated product and the standard earplug.. Decision rule: If the difference in purchase intent between the differentiated product and the standard earplug is at least 1.5 points (e.g., differentiated intent ≥ 7.5 and standard intent ≤ 6), proceed to develop a differentiated consumer proposition. Sample: 500 adults aged 18-45, recruited via an online panel, balanced across the two groups (250 per group).. Measure: Purchase intent (binary: would buy) and willingness to pay (EUR). Secondary measure: stated reason for purchase (lifestyle vs compliance).. Predictions: T1: Group A will show purchase intent at least 20% higher than Group B.; T2: Group B will show purchase intent at least 20% higher than Group A.. Decision rule: If Group A’s purchase intent is at least 20% higher than Group B, proceed with a differentiated lifestyle proposition (supports T1). Sample: 500 respondents: 250 self-identified outdoor/recreation enthusiasts and 250 self-identified professional/industrial users.. Measure: 1) Purchase intent (binary: would buy). 2) Primary reason for purchase (open-ended). 3) Maximum price willing to pay (EUR).. Predictions: T1: Enthusiast group will show higher purchase intent and cite enjoyment of activities as primary reason, with willingness to pay at least 20% above standard industrial earplug price.; T2: Professional group will show higher purchase intent and cite compliance requirements as primary reason, with willingness to pay at least 15% above standard industrial earplug price.. Decision rule: If enthusiast group purchase intent >= 40% and compliance reason < 20% of responses, proceed to develop a lifestyle proposition. If professional group purchase intent >= 40% and compliance reason < 20% of responses, proceed to develop a compliance proposition. If neither condition is met, do not expand.. Cost: 18000 euros, 10 weeks.

Test "Consumer vs Small-Farm Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups: Group A receives a consumer-focused proposition emphasizing convenience, single-tool functionality, and homeowner benefits; Group B receives a small-farm-focused proposition emphasizing versatility, multiple task capability, and small-farm owner benefits. Both groups are shown a product description of a differentiated lawn tractor (e.g., Deere 4010) and asked to indicate purchase intent on a 7-point scale (1‑10).. Sample: 500 participants: 250 homeowners with small gardens and 250 small-farm owners. Recruited via online panels to ensure demographic representation.. Measure: Purchase intent score (1‑10) for each group.. Predictions: T1: Group A will have a higher average purchase intent score than Group B.; T2: Group B will have a higher average purchase intent score than Group A.. Decision rule: If the difference in average purchase intent scores between Group A and Group B is at least 1.5 points (e.g., Group A average ≥ 5.5 and Group B average ≤ 4.0), conclude the differentiated proposition aligns with the respective theory and justify investment. If the difference is less than 1.5 points, indicate uncertainty and recommend further market research.. Cost: 15000 euros, 6 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition for homeowners with small gardens, leveraging the existing tractor engineering to create a single-tool lawn tractor. This aligns with the 76% rise in lawn and garden equipment sales and the established B2B2C model of independent dealer distribution. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

T1 kept: Simulated evidence SYN-D concerns a warehouse label printer and does not address consumer demand, homeowner behavior, or small-farm owner preferences. Therefore it does not affect the validity of T1. New claim: none. Evidence: SYN-D.

Recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition for homeowners with small gardens, leveraging the existing tractor engineering to create a single-tool lawn tractor. This aligns with the 76% rise in lawn and garden equipment sales and the established B2B2C model of independent dealer distribution. Target customer: Homeowners with small gardens who need a single, convenient tool for mowing, weeding, and light landscaping.. Value proposition: A differentiated lawn tractor that combines the durability and performance of a Deere tractor with a user-friendly design, offering a single tool for multiple tasks and reducing the need for multiple equipment purchases.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed Consumer vs Small-Farm Messaging Test to validate purchase intent differences and determine whether to proceed with product development.. Uncertainty: The willingness of homeowners to pay a premium for a differentiated proposition is uncertain. The test will clarify whether purchase intent is driven by consumer convenience or small-farm versatility.. Would change if: If the test shows a difference in purchase intent of less than 1.5 points between the consumer and small-farm messages, indicating insufficient evidence to justify investment.; If new evidence shows strong demand for small-farm owners specifically, shifting the recommendation toward a small-farm proposition.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Test "Consumer vs Small-Farm Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups: Group A receives a consumer-focused proposition for small-scale landscaping (e.g., 'The Deere Lawn Tractor: One tool for mowing, weeding, and light landscaping.') Group B receives a small-farm focused proposition for versatile agricultural and garden tasks (e.g., 'The Deere Lawn Tractor: A single tool for mowing, weeding, and light landscaping, built for durability and reliability.') Both groups see the same product description and price point.. Sample: 500 participants: 250 homeowners with small gardens and 250 small-farm owners. Recruited via online panels to ensure geographic diversity.. Measure: Purchase intent measured on a 7-point Likert scale (1 = very unlikely, 7 = very likely) and willingness to pay a premium (percentage willing to pay at least 10% more than the base price).. Predictions: T1: Group A will show higher purchase intent and willingness to pay a premium than Group B.; T2: Group B will show higher purchase intent and willingness to pay a premium than Group A.. Decision rule: If the average purchase intent for Group A is at least 1.5 points higher than Group B and the difference is statistically significant (p < 0.05), conclude T1 is more likely. If Group B's average purchase intent is at least 1.5 points higher and the difference is statistically significant, conclude T2 is more likely. If neither difference meets the threshold, the test is inconclusive and no expansion is recommended.. Cost: 15000 euros, 6 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition for small-scale landscaping, leveraging Deere’s tractor engineering to offer a single, integrated tool for mowing, weeding, and light landscaping. This aligns with the 1962 lawn equipment sales surge and the existing consumer market entry, and it provides a clear use case for homeowners. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition for small-scale landscaping, leveraging Deere’s tractor engineering to offer a single, integrated tool for mowing, weeding, and light landscaping. This aligns with the 1962 lawn equipment sales surge and the existing consumer market entry, and it provides a clear use case for homeowners. Target customer: Individual homeowners with small gardens who need a single tool for mowing, weeding, and light landscaping.. Value proposition: A differentiated lawn tractor that combines the durability and reliability of a tractor with the convenience of a single tool, reducing the need for multiple devices and saving time and effort.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed Consumer vs Small-Farm Messaging Test to validate purchase intent and willingness to pay for the differentiated proposition.. Uncertainty: The willingness of homeowners to pay a premium for a differentiated lawn tractor is uncertain. The test will clarify whether purchase intent and willingness to pay are driven by consumer or small-farm messaging.. Would change if: If the test shows that small-farm owners express higher purchase intent and willingness to pay than homeowners, the recommendation would shift to a small-farm focused proposition.; If neither group meets the purchase intent threshold, the recommendation would remain to maintain the current B2B2C model without expansion.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Test "Consumer vs Small-Farm Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups: Group A receives a consumer-focused message emphasizing convenience, affordability, and ease of use for small gardens; Group B receives a small-farm-focused message emphasizing labor cost savings, efficiency, and suitability for light-to-moderate farming tasks. Both groups view a generic farm tractor model and are asked to indicate purchase intent on a 7-point scale (1‑10).. Sample: 300 participants: 150 homeowners with small gardens and 150 small-farm owners. Recruited via an online panel to ensure demographic representation.. Measure: Purchase intent score (1‑10) for the assigned message.. Test "Consumer Proposition Test: Status vs. Utility" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with simulated purchase offer. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups: Group A (status-oriented) and Group B (utility-oriented). Each group sees a product description of a differentiated consumer lawn tractor (e.g., a branded, feature-rich unit) and is asked to indicate purchase intent (1‑10 scale) and maximum price they would pay. The test also includes a control group receiving a generic tractor description.. Sample: 300 participants, 100 per group, recruited from a panel of homeowners and small gardeners in the United States. Recruitment is limited to those who have owned a lawn tractor or plan to purchase one within the next 12 months.. Measure: Purchase intent score (1‑10) and maximum price willingness to pay for the differentiated unit.. Predictions: T1: Group A will show higher purchase intent and higher willingness to pay than Group B, indicating that status-driven demand drives purchase.; T2: Group B will show higher purchase intent and higher willingness to pay than Group A, indicating that status-driven demand drives purchase.. Decision rule: If the average purchase intent score for Group A is at least 5 points higher than Group B (i.e., Group A’s average ≥ 7.5 and Group B’s average ≤ 2.5), conclude that status-driven demand (T2) is the dominant driver. If the difference is less than 5 points, conclude that utility-driven demand (T1) is the dominant driver. If both groups’ average scores are within 5 points of each other, the test is inconclusive and further data is needed.. Cost: 20000 euros, 12 weeks.

Why behaviour changes: Buyers will shift from generic emergency equipment to a dedicated beacon when they understand its unique capability to reach a distress call through satellite, offering peace of mind and higher perceived safety.. How value is captured: ACR can capture value by selling premium-priced units directly to consumers through outdoor retailers or online channels, leveraging its existing brand credibility for marine and military safety.. Assumptions: Consumers are aware of the existence and purpose of 406 MHz PLBs.; Outdoor activities in remote areas (e.g., Alaska, Australia) are common enough to create demand.; Willingness to pay a premium for a specialized device is higher than for generic ELTs.; ACR can reach individual buyers through existing channels or new partnerships.. Predictions: In a test offering a consumer-focused marketing campaign to outdoor groups, purchase intent will exceed 10% among respondents who identify themselves as hikers, campers, or boating recreationists.; Surveyed consumers will cite 'safety in remote emergencies' as the top reason for purchasing the beacon, with willingness to pay at least $800..

T2: Individual buyers will adopt a consumer-grade 406 MHz satellite distress beacon primarily because it is marketed as a cost-effective, no‑regulation alternative to expensive ELTs and RFFI, and they will purchase it when price is the primary barrier to entry. Who benefits: Budget‑conscious outdoor enthusiasts, boat owners, and emergency‑prepared individuals who need a reliable signaling device without the cost of professional certification.. Why behaviour changes: Buyers will switch from generic emergency equipment to a dedicated beacon when they perceive it as a cheaper, simpler solution that meets the same safety requirement without the regulatory and certification overhead.. How value is captured: ACR can capture value by selling lower‑priced units through mass‑market channels, leveraging its existing manufacturing capabilities to produce a consumer‑focused version of its existing product line.. Assumptions: Price is the primary barrier to adoption for emergency signaling devices.; Consumers are aware of the existence of 406 MHz PLBs but do not view them as a premium product.; ACR can produce a consumer‑grade version of its existing product at a lower cost than its current B2B offerings.. Predictions: In a test offering a low‑priced consumer version of the beacon, purchase intent will be higher among respondents who cite budget constraints as their primary reason for not buying a beacon.; Surveyed consumers will cite 'cost' as the top reason for not purchasing a beacon, with willingness to pay at least $500..

T1 supports, from acr-fr-purpose (regulation): "The 406 MHz PLB is primarily intended to provide a distress and alerting capacity for use by the general public in life threatening situations in a remote environment after all other means of notifying SAR responders (e.g., telephone, radio) have been exhausted.". Does not show: It does not show that consumers will purchase the device or that they will pay a premium for it; it only defines the device's purpose and intended use..

T2 supports, from acr-wiki-epirbcost (market_fact): "Emergency Position-Indicating Radio Beacons (EPIRBs) are a development of the ELT designed specifically for use on boats and ships, and basic models tend to be less expensive than ELTs (average cost is $800". Does not show: It does not show that consumers will purchase the device or that price is the primary barrier; it only indicates the price range of existing ELTs..

Test "Consumer Messaging Test: Premium vs. Cost-Concern Messaging" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging condition. Recruit 400 respondents (200 self-identified outdoor enthusiasts/hikers, 200 budget-conscious consumers). Randomly assign participants to one of two message conditions: (A) premium positioning emphasizing life-saving capability and remote emergency use; (B) cost‑concern positioning emphasizing lower price and no certification requirement. Both conditions present a $800 price point for a consumer‑grade 406 MHz beacon. Measure purchase intent (binary: "Would buy") and primary reason for not buying (open‑ended).. Sample: 400 respondents (200 outdoor enthusiasts, 200 budget‑conscious consumers) recruited via outdoor forums and general consumer panels.. Measure: Purchase intent (binary) and primary reason for not buying (open‑ended).. Predictions: T1: In the premium condition, purchase intent will be at least 10% among outdoor enthusiasts and at least 5% among budget‑conscious consumers; primary reason will be "safety in remote emergencies."; T2: In the cost‑concern condition, purchase intent will be at least 10% among budget‑conscious consumers and at least 5% among outdoor enthusiasts; primary reason will be "cost.". Decision rule: If purchase intent in the premium condition exceeds 10% among outdoor enthusiasts and 5% among budget‑conscious consumers, proceed to develop a differentiated consumer proposition. If purchase intent in the cost‑concern condition exceeds 10% among budget‑conscious consumers and 5% among outdoor enthusiasts, consider a lower‑priced consumer version. If neither condition meets its threshold, do not expand into consumer sales.. Cost: 18000 euros, 10 weeks.

Favours T1: Do not invest in a differentiated consumer proposition at this time. Public sources from 2002 indicate the 406 MHz PLB is intended for life‑threatening remote emergencies and is regulated for general public use, but there is no evidence of consumer demand, willingness to pay, or market feasibility. The proposed test (X1) would be needed to validate whether consumers will adopt a premium, life‑saving positioning. Beliefs: T1: uncertain; T2: unlikely.

Recommendation: Do not invest in a differentiated consumer proposition at this time. Public sources from 2002 indicate the 406 MHz PLB is intended for life‑threatening remote emergencies and is regulated for general public use, but there is no evidence of consumer demand, willingness to pay, or market feasibility. The proposed test (X1) would be needed to validate whether consumers will adopt a premium, life‑saving positioning. Target customer: Individual outdoor enthusiasts and recreational users who need reliable signaling in remote areas where traditional communication fails.. Value proposition: A differentiated consumer product positioned as a premium safety tool for remote emergencies, leveraging ACR’s existing brand credibility for marine and military safety.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed Consumer Messaging Test (X1) to measure purchase intent under premium and cost‑concern messaging conditions.. Uncertainty: The size of the consumer market, willingness to pay a premium, and ACR’s ability to reach individual buyers through existing channels remain uncertain.. Would change if: If the test shows purchase intent in the premium condition exceeds 10% among outdoor enthusiasts and 5% among budget‑conscious consumers, we would proceed to develop a differentiated consumer proposition.; If the test shows purchase intent in the cost‑concern condition exceeds 10% among budget‑conscious consumers and 5% among outdoor enthusiasts, we would consider a lower‑priced consumer version.; If neither condition meets its threshold, we would maintain the current focus on B2B customers and existing product portfolio.. Beliefs: T1: uncertain; T2: unlikely.

Test "Consumer Preference Test: Health Monitoring vs Fitness Tracking" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized exposure to two product concepts: (1) Health Monitoring Scale - marketed as a body-fat tracking device providing measurable insights (e.g., fat percentage, fat distribution). (2) Fitness Tracking Scale - marketed as a real-time activity and weight loss tracking device.. Sample: 500 adults aged 18-55, recruited from a panel in Japan and the United States, balanced for gender and BMI to reflect target markets.. Measure: Purchase intent measured on a 7-point Likert scale (1 = very unlikely, 7 = very likely) and willingness to pay (WTP) in euros.. Predictions: T1: Higher purchase intent and WTP for the Health Monitoring Scale compared to the Fitness Tracking Scale.; T2: Higher purchase intent and WTP for the Fitness Tracking Scale compared to the Health Monitoring Scale.. Decision rule: If the average purchase intent for the Health Monitoring Scale exceeds the average purchase intent for the Fitness Tracking Scale by at least 1.5 points on the 7-point scale, proceed with a differentiated consumer proposition focused on health monitoring. If the difference is less than 1.5 points, conduct a follow-up test to explore the fitness tracking concept.. Cost: 15000 euros, 6 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition that positions the home body-fat scale as a health monitoring tool, providing measurable insights into body fat distribution. This aligns with existing consumer behavior in Japan and the accuracy of the Tanita device, while leaving room for a follow-up test to explore fitness tracking if demand is not strong enough. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition that positions the home body-fat scale as a health monitoring tool, providing measurable insights into body fat distribution. This aligns with existing consumer behavior in Japan and the accuracy of the Tanita device, while leaving room for a follow-up test to explore fitness tracking if demand is not strong enough. Target customer: Health-conscious consumers aged 18-55 who seek to monitor weight and body composition at home.. Value proposition: A premium home body-fat scale that delivers clear, actionable health insights, enabling users to track progress and make informed decisions about their health.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed Consumer Preference Test (500 adults, 6 weeks, €15,000) to compare health-monitoring and fitness-tracking concepts. Use the decision rule: if health-monitoring intent exceeds fitness-tracking intent by ≥1.5 points, proceed;. Uncertainty: The test will determine whether consumers are willing to pay a premium for health insights. If the difference is <1.5 points, the fitness-tracking concept may be more viable.. Would change if: If the test shows a ≥1.5-point advantage for fitness-tracking intent, we would shift focus to a fitness-tracking differentiated product.; If no test is run, we would proceed with a health-monitoring proposition based on existing consumer behavior and device accuracy.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Test "Willingness-to-Pay Survey for Home-Studio Creators" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with a choice-based conjoint design. Participants are recruited from home-studio creators and individual audio enthusiasts. They view product descriptions of Neumann studio microphones and studio monitors, and are asked to indicate their maximum price they would pay for each product, and to rank importance of brand reputation (high, medium, low) and importance of reliability (high, medium, low).. Sample: 300 participants: 150 home-studio creators (self-identified) and 150 individual buyers (non-creators). Recruit via audio forums, social media, and email lists.. Measure: 1) Maximum price participants would pay for each product (binary: would pay or would not pay). 2) Importance ratings for brand reputation and reliability (Likert scale 1-5).. Predictions: T1: Creators will show higher willingness to pay for Neumann products when brand reputation is rated high, and lower willingness to pay when reliability is rated high.; T2: Creators will show higher willingness to pay for Neumann products when reliability is rated high, and lower willingness to pay when brand reputation is rated high.. Decision rule: If the average willingness-to-pay for Neumann products is at least 20% higher when brand reputation is rated high than when reliability is rated high, conclude T1 is more supported. If the average willingness-to-pay is at least 20% higher when reliability is rated high than when brand reputation is rated high, conclude T2 is more supported. If neither difference is statistically significant (p < 0.05), the theories are not differentiated.. Cost: 2000 euros, 4 weeks.

Test "Framing Test for Home Body-Fat Analyser" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging. Participants are recruited from a panel of health-conscious adults (n=300). Participants are randomly assigned to one of two conditions: Health Framing (device marketed as a health monitoring tool for weight management) or Fitness Framing (device marketed as a fitness tracking device). Both conditions present the same product description and price (proposed €199). Participants indicate purchase intent (1‑10 scale) and willingness to pay (1‑10 euros).. Sample: 300 health-conscious adults recruited online, balanced for age, gender, and BMI.. Measure: Purchase intent (binary) and willingness to pay (continuous).. Predictions: T1: Higher purchase intent and willingness to pay in the Health Framing condition compared to the Fitness Framing condition.; T2: Higher purchase intent and willingness to pay in the Fitness Framing condition compared to the Health Framing condition.. Decision rule: If the average purchase intent in the Health Framing condition is at least 10 points higher than in the Fitness Framing condition (p < 0.05), recommend developing a differentiated consumer proposition focused on health monitoring. If the difference is less than 10 points, recommend no expansion and continue focusing on the current B2B market.. Cost: 20000 euros, 12 weeks.

Favours T1: Develop a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case (health monitoring) rather than a broad fitness or general consumer offering. The evidence shows that consumers already use bathroom scales and keep track of body composition, and the company already markets a professional body-fat analyser. A health-focused framing aligns with existing consumer behavior and provides a clear value proposition. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Recommendation: Develop a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case (health monitoring) rather than a broad fitness or general consumer offering. The evidence shows that consumers already use bathroom scales and keep track of body composition, and the company already markets a professional body-fat analyser. A health-focused framing aligns with existing consumer behavior and provides a clear value proposition. Target customer: Health-conscious adults who already use bathroom scales and seek measurable health data for weight management.. Value proposition: A home body-fat analyser marketed as a health monitoring tool, providing a clear, measurable body-fat percentage to help users track weight and make informed health decisions.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed framing test (300 health-conscious adults, randomized messaging, purchase intent and willingness to pay) to validate the health-framing hypothesis before committing to product development.. Uncertainty: The test will determine whether consumers will pay a premium for a health-focused device and whether the framing difference is statistically significant. Without the test, the demand for a consumer proposition remains uncertain.. Would change if: If the framing test shows the Fitness Framing condition outperforms the Health Framing condition by at least 10 points (p < 0.05), we would reconsider the consumer proposition and explore a fitness-focused approach.; If the test shows no significant difference between framing conditions, we would recommend no expansion and continue focusing on the current B2B market.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Why behaviour changes: When appearance is a barrier, free distribution removes the cost and stigma, making protection accessible without feeling mandatory.. Assumptions: Appearance is a significant barrier for a segment of users.; Free distribution lowers the perceived cost of acquisition.; Fashion retailers are willing to stock specialized, stylish hearing protection.. Test "Appearance vs Compliance Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging condition. Participants are recruited from two segments: fashion-conscious consumers (n=200) and workplace safety professionals (n=200). Each segment is randomly assigned to one of two message conditions: (A) stylish, fashion-focused messaging emphasizing appearance and style; (B) functional, compliance-focused messaging emphasizing workplace safety standards and regulatory compliance. Participants are asked to indicate their willingness to purchase a free pair of earplugs for a specific use case (e.g., concerts, outdoor recreation, construction).. Sample: 400 participants (200 fashion-conscious consumers, 200 workplace safety professionals).. Measure: Willingness to purchase a free pair of earplugs on a 7-point scale (1 = very unlikely, 7 = very likely).. Predictions: T1: Fashion-conscious participants will show higher willingness to purchase under stylish messaging than under compliance messaging.; T2: Workplace safety professionals will show higher willingness to purchase under compliance messaging than under stylish messaging.. Decision rule: If the average willingness to purchase for the stylish condition is at least 1.5 points higher than for the compliance condition among fashion-conscious participants, proceed to develop a differentiated consumer proposition emphasizing appearance. If the average willingness to purchase for the compliance condition is at least 1.5 points higher than for the stylish condition among workplace safety professionals, proceed to develop a differentiated consumer proposition emphasizing compliance. If neither difference is statistically significant, do not invest in a differentiated consumer proposition.. Cost: 18000 euros, 10 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition that positions hearing protection as a stylish, fashion accessory, particularly for fashion-conscious users. Use free distribution and fashion retail partnerships to test demand before broader rollout. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Uncertainty: The primary uncertainty is whether appearance is the dominant barrier for consumers, and whether free distribution alone drives adoption. The test will resolve this.. Would change if: If the test shows compliance messaging (T2) generates at least 1.5 points higher willingness than stylish messaging, we would shift focus to workplace safety positioning.; If neither condition shows a significant difference, we would reconsider expansion or no expansion.; If new evidence shows strong regulatory compliance demand (e.g., EN 352 standards) as the primary driver, we would strengthen compliance positioning.. Test "Consumer vs Small-Farm Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups: Group A receives a homeowner-focused lawn tractor proposition emphasizing convenience, single-tool solution, and brand trust; Group B receives a small-farm owner-focused proposition emphasizing versatility, multiple task capability, and brand reputation. Both groups see the same product description and price point.. Sample: 500 participants: 250 homeowners (recruited via homeowner panels) and 250 small-farm owners (recruited via agricultural forums and small-farm owner networks). Stratify by region to ensure geographic diversity.. Measure: Purchase intent measured on a 7-point Likert scale (1 = very unlikely, 7 = very likely) and binary purchase decision (would buy). Secondary measure: stated willingness to pay a premium over a generic garden tool.. Predictions: T1: Group A will show higher purchase intent and willingness to pay a premium than Group B.; T2: Group B will show higher purchase intent and willingness to pay a premium than Group A.. Decision rule: If the difference in average purchase intent between the two groups is at least 1.5 points on the 7-point scale, we conclude the theory is supported. If the difference is less than 1.5 points, we conclude neither theory is supported. If both groups show similar intent, we conclude the test is inconclusive and further evidence is needed.. Cost: 8000 euros, 6 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition for homeowners, leveraging the existing tractor engineering to create a single-tool lawn tractor that offers convenience, durability, and brand trust. This aligns with the observed 76% rise in lawn and garden equipment sales and the popularity of the 4010 model, indicating a growing homeowner market. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

T1 kept: The simulated result (SYN-D) concerns a warehouse label printer and does not address homeowner or small-farm owner demand for a differentiated lawn tractor proposition. Therefore it bears on neither T1 nor T2 and does not change the theory. New claim: none. Evidence: SYN-D.

Recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition for homeowners, leveraging the existing tractor engineering to create a single-tool lawn tractor that emphasizes convenience, durability, and brand trust. This aligns with the observed 76% rise in lawn and garden equipment sales and the popularity of the 4010 model, indicating a growing homeowner market. Target customer: Individual homeowners with small gardens who need a single tool for mowing, weeding, and light landscaping.. Value proposition: A differentiated lawn tractor that combines the performance and reliability of a Deere tractor with a user-friendly design, offering a convenient, all-in-one solution for homeowner tasks.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed Consumer vs Small-Farm Messaging Test (or a similar survey experiment) to validate purchase intent and willingness to pay for the differentiated proposition.. Uncertainty: The size of the homeowner market and their willingness to pay a premium for a differentiated proposition are uncertain. Competitor lawn tractors and the potential for small-farm owner demand also remain uncertain.. Would change if: If the test shows purchase intent for the differentiated proposition is significantly lower than for a generic garden tool, we would reconsider the investment.; If new evidence shows small-farm owners are the primary drivers of lawn tractor demand, we would shift focus to a small-farm proposition.; If the market size for small gardens is smaller than expected, we would limit production and marketing to homeowners.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Test "Fashion vs Safety Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging condition. Participants are recruited from a panel of adults aged 18-45, screened for prior purchase of hearing protection. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two conditions: Condition A (fashion-focused) or Condition B (safety-focused). In Condition A, the product is described as a stylish, fashion-branded earplug for concerts and outdoor activities, emphasizing comfort and discreet design. In Condition B, the product is described as a safety-certified earplug for high-risk activities (construction, hunting, medical), emphasizing EN 352 certification and proven performance. Both conditions include a willingness-to-pay (WTP) question and a purchase intent question.. Sample: 400 participants (200 per condition), recruited from an online panel to ensure diversity in age, gender, and geographic location.. Measure: Purchase intent (binary: would purchase) and maximum willingness-to-pay (EUR). Secondary measure: intent to purchase multiple pairs for different activities.. Predictions: T1: Condition A will show higher purchase intent and higher WTP than Condition B.; T2: Condition B will show higher purchase intent and higher WTP than Condition A.. Decision rule: If Condition A purchase intent ≥ 40% and Condition B purchase intent ≤ 30%, conclude T1 is supported. If Condition B purchase intent ≥ 40% and Condition A purchase intent ≤ 30%, conclude T2 is supported. If neither condition meets its threshold, conclude neither theory is supported. If both conditions meet their thresholds, conduct a secondary test to separate the two.. Cost: 8000 euros, 4 weeks.

Test "Consumer Messaging Test: Marine vs Residential" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups: Marine Group (Jotun’s marine and protective coatings) or Residential Group (Jotun’s decorative and protective coatings). Each group sees a product description and a price point. The Marine Group also sees a brief explanation of Jotun’s marine technology and brand reputation. The Residential Group sees the same product description and price point without the marine explanation. Both groups are asked about purchase intent (1‑10 scale) and willingness to pay a premium (if any).. Sample: 500 respondents: 250 marine enthusiasts and 250 homeowners, recruited via online panels to ensure geographic diversity.. Measure: Purchase intent score (1‑10) and willingness to pay a premium (percentage willing to pay more than the baseline price).. Predictions: T1: Marine Group will show higher purchase intent and willingness to pay a premium than Residential Group.; T2: Residential Group will show higher purchase intent and willingness to pay a premium than Marine Group.. Decision rule: If the average purchase intent for Marine Group is at least 5 points higher than for Residential Group (i.e., Marine ≥ 5.5 and Residential < 5.5), conclude T1 is supported. If the difference is less than 5 points, conclude neither theory is strongly supported. If both groups’ intent scores are within 5 points of each other, conclude no significant difference.. Cost: 2000 euros, 4 weeks.

Favours T1: Jotun should invest in a differentiated consumer proposition for marine enthusiasts, leveraging its marine and protective coatings technology to capture premium pricing and direct-to-consumer sales. This aligns with existing direct-to-consumer capabilities and the brand’s reputation for performance. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

T1 kept: The simulated result concerns a warehouse label printer and does not address consumer demand, purchase behavior, or the specific theories T1 or T2. Therefore it does not affect the conclusions about marine enthusiasts or homeowners purchasing Jotun products. New claim: none. Evidence: SYN-D.

Recommendation: Jotun should invest in a differentiated consumer proposition for marine enthusiasts, leveraging its marine and protective coatings technology to capture premium pricing and direct-to-consumer sales. Target customer: Marine enthusiasts and boat owners who value performance, durability, and brand reputation.. Value proposition: Jotun’s marine coatings offer superior protection and durability, backed by a trusted brand, allowing marine enthusiasts to achieve long‑term performance and safety for their vessels.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Conduct the proposed Consumer Messaging Test to measure purchase intent and willingness to pay a premium for marine versus residential messaging, and use the results to decide whether to launch a differentiated marine consumer proposition.. Uncertainty: The size of the marine enthusiast market and their willingness to pay a premium for Jotun’s products are uncertain. Additionally, the strength of direct-to-consumer sales through Jotun’s website remains unproven.. Would change if: If the Consumer Messaging Test shows that homeowners express higher purchase intent and willingness to pay a premium than marine enthusiasts, the recommendation would shift toward a broader residential consumer proposition.; If new evidence shows that marine enthusiasts are not purchasing through Jotun’s website or that the marine market is smaller than expected, the investment would be reconsidered.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Test "Fashion vs Safety Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging condition. Participants are recruited from a panel of adults interested in hearing protection. Each participant sees one of two product descriptions for a hearing protection earplug: (A) Positioned as a fashion accessory and comfort item (e.g., "Stylish, comfortable earplugs for everyday use"); (B) Positioned as a safety requirement for a specific activity (e.g., "Compliant with EN 352 for construction and outdoor recreation"). They are then asked to indicate purchase intent on a 7-point scale (1‑10) and maximum price they would pay.. Sample: 300 participants (150 per condition) to ensure statistical power.. Measure: Purchase intent score (1‑10) and maximum price willingness to pay for each condition.. Predictions: T1: Condition A will yield a higher average purchase intent score and higher willingness to pay than Condition B.; T2: Condition B will yield a higher average purchase intent score and higher willingness to pay than Condition A.. Decision rule: If Condition A’s average purchase intent score is at least 1.5 points higher than Condition B’s, conclude T1 is supported. If Condition B’s average purchase intent score is at least 1.5 points higher than Condition A’s, conclude T2 is supported. If the difference is less than 1.5 points, the test is inconclusive and further research is needed.. Cost: 2000 euros, 4 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition that emphasizes fashion and comfort, targeting everyday users and leisure activities. Use design and marketing that highlights style and comfort to overcome perceived discomfort and appearance concerns. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

events.text: Objective: Determine whether there is sufficient public evidence to justify Hellberg Safety investing in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case beyond its current hearing-protection offering.. Constraints: Limited to publicly available information; no internal company data.; Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeline for any proposed experiment.; Must identify evidence of consumer demand, willingness to pay, and competitive positioning.; Must consider existing B2B relationships and current reach to individual buyers.. Alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition targeting a specific use case (e.g., outdoor recreation, construction, medical).; 2) Expand the existing hearing-protection line into adjacent consumer segments without differentiation (e.g., standard earplugs for general use).; 3) No expansion: continue focusing on existing B2B hearing and face protection markets.; 4) Change route to market or customer group (e.g., sell directly to consumers online, partner with retailers, target a new demographic).; 5) Redesign existing products for a new use case (e.g., add comfort features for extended wear)..

T1: Consumers will adopt a differentiated consumer proposition if they perceive it as a safety necessity for a specific use case (e.g., outdoor recreation, medical). They will pay a premium for products that meet or exceed regulatory standards (EN 352) and offer comfort and situational awareness. Who benefits: Individual consumers who need reliable hearing protection for specific activities (hunters, shooters, children, workers).. Why behaviour changes: Regulatory requirements and the need for reliable protection create a demand for certified products; comfort and situational awareness reduce perceived discomfort, making the product desirable beyond basic compliance.. How value is captured: Hellberg can capture value by pricing differentiated products at a premium, selling through specialized channels (outdoor retailers, online), and leveraging its brand reputation for safety and comfort.. Assumptions: Consumers are aware of and understand EN 352 standards.; Regulatory compliance is a key purchase driver for hearing protection.; Comfort and situational awareness are important attributes for extended wear.. Predictions: In a test offering a differentiated product for a specific use case, purchase intent will be higher than for a standard earplug.; Willingness to pay will be above the price of a standard earplug, indicating a premium..

T2: Consumers will adopt a differentiated consumer proposition if they perceive it as a lifestyle or fashion accessory, especially for children and outdoor enthusiasts. They will choose products that are visible, shareable, and align with personal style, leading to multiple purchases. Who benefits: Individual consumers who value personal style and social sharing, particularly parents of children and outdoor enthusiasts.. Why behaviour changes: Social media and peer influence make visible, shareable products more attractive; children and outdoor users seek products that stand out and are easy to show off, increasing purchase frequency.. How value is captured: Hellberg can capture value by designing visually appealing, shareable products, selling through lifestyle retailers and online platforms, and leveraging social media marketing to build brand awareness.. Assumptions: Social media and peer influence significantly impact purchase decisions for hearing protection.; Parents and outdoor enthusiasts are willing to pay a premium for stylish, visible products.; Products can be marketed as fashion accessories rather than purely functional safety gear.. Predictions: In a test offering a differentiated product positioned as a fashion accessory, purchase intent will be higher than for a standard earplug.; Willingness to pay will be above the price of a standard earplug, indicating a premium for style..

Test "Differentiated vs Standard Earplug Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized product exposure. Participants are randomly assigned to view either a differentiated product for a specific use case (e.g., outdoor recreation) or a standard earplug. Both products are presented with the same price point (proposed €30). Participants indicate purchase intent (1‑10 scale) and maximum willingness to pay (WTP).. Sample: 300 adult consumers recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and geographic region to ensure representativeness.. Measure: Purchase intent score and WTP for the differentiated product versus the standard earplug.. Predictions: T1: Higher purchase intent and WTP for the differentiated product than for the standard earplug.; T2: No significant difference in purchase intent and WTP between the differentiated product and the standard earplug.. Decision rule: If the difference in purchase intent between the differentiated product and the standard earplug is at least 1.5 points (e.g., differentiated intent ≥ 7.5 and standard intent ≤ 6), proceed to develop a differentiated consumer proposition. If the difference is less than 1.5 points, do not invest in a differentiated proposition and continue focusing on existing B2B markets.. Cost: 18000 euros, 10 weeks.

Test "Lifestyle vs. Compliance Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two conditions: Lifestyle Condition (message emphasizing style, activity alignment, and fashion-forward design) or Compliance Condition (message emphasizing safety standards, activity-specific protection, and compliance requirements). Both conditions present a standard earplug product at a fixed price point.. Sample: 300 adult consumers recruited via an online panel, balanced across the two conditions (150 per condition). Recruitment targets individuals who engage in outdoor activities (hunting, shooting, cycling) and those who value personal style.. Measure: Purchase intent measured on a 7-point Likert scale (1 = very unlikely, 7 = very likely). Secondary measure: stated primary reason for choosing the product (style/activity alignment vs. safety/compliance).. Predictions: T1: In the Lifestyle Condition, purchase intent will be at least 15% higher than in the Compliance Condition.; T2: In the Compliance Condition, purchase intent will be at least 15% higher than in the Lifestyle Condition.. Decision rule: If the difference in purchase intent between the Lifestyle and Compliance conditions is at least 15 percentage points, proceed with a differentiated consumer proposition targeting lifestyle/activity alignment. If the difference is less than 15 points, do not invest in a differentiated proposition and focus on existing B2B markets.. Cost: 18000 euros, 10 weeks.

Test "Certified vs. Tracked 406 MHz Beacon Purchase Intent Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with simulated purchase scenarios. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups: Group A sees a certified 406 MHz beacon described as meeting NOAA/RTCM standards and marketed for marine recreational use; Group B sees the same beacon described as offering real-time tracking and rescue notifications, marketed for outdoor workers and families. Both groups see the same product price (proposed €150). Participants indicate purchase intent on a 7-point scale (1 = very unlikely, 7 = very likely).. Sample: 300 respondents: 150 marine recreational users and 150 outdoor workers/families, recruited via online panels to match demographic distribution of target segments.. Measure: Purchase intent score for each group (mean of 7-point scale).. Predictions: T1: Group A will have a mean purchase intent score at least 1.5 points higher than Group B (i.e., ≥5.5 on the 7-point scale).; T2: Group B will have a mean purchase intent score at least 1.5 points higher than Group A (i.e., ≥5.5 on the 7-point scale).. Decision rule: If Group A's mean purchase intent score is at least 1.5 points higher than Group B's, conclude T1 is more supported. If Group B's mean purchase intent score is at least 1.5 points higher than Group A's, conclude T2 is more supported. If the difference is less than 1.5 points, the test is inconclusive and further data is needed.. Cost: 18000 euros, 10 weeks.

Test "Differentiated vs Certified Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging exposure. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two conditions: Condition A receives a lifestyle positioning message (stylish, comfortable, fashion accessory) and a free entry-point provision message; Condition B receives a safety-requirement positioning message (high-risk activity, mandatory certification) and a free entry-point provision message. Both conditions include a purchase intent question and a willingness-to-pay question.. Sample: 500 adults aged 18-45 recruited via an online panel, balanced across the two conditions to ensure random assignment.. Measure: Purchase intent (binary: would buy) and maximum willingness-to-pay (EUR).. Predictions: T1: Condition A will show purchase intent at least 20% higher than Condition B.; T2: Condition B will show purchase intent at least 20% higher than Condition A.. Decision rule: If Condition A purchase intent ≥ 20% and Condition B purchase intent < 20%, conclude T1 is supported. If Condition B purchase intent ≥ 20% and Condition A purchase intent < 20%, conclude T2 is supported. If neither condition meets its threshold, conclude neither theory is supported. If both conditions meet their thresholds, conduct a secondary test to separate the two mechanisms.. Cost: 2000 euros, 4 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition that positions hearing protection as a stylish, comfortable lifestyle accessory, particularly for high-risk activities where free entry-point provision is feasible. Recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition that positions hearing protection as a stylish, comfortable lifestyle accessory, particularly for high-risk activities where free entry-point provision is feasible. Begin with a small-scale pilot offering the product at concert doors to test purchase intent and willingness to pay. Target customer: Adults aged 18-45 who attend concerts, outdoor recreation, and leisure activities and currently view hearing protection as a medical necessity.. Value proposition: A hearing-protection product that combines comfort, style, and safety, marketed as a fashion accessory for specific activities, providing peace of mind and meeting EN 352 standards.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed Differentiated vs Certified Messaging Test (Condition A vs Condition B) to validate purchase intent differences and determine whether lifestyle positioning or safety messaging drives adoption.. Uncertainty: The size of the consumer market for hearing protection and the willingness to pay for a differentiated product are unknown. Evidence of free entry-point provision and consumer demand for stylish protection is limited to studies linking free. Would change if: If the test shows Condition A purchase intent below 20% or Condition B purchase intent above 20%, the recommendation would shift to focus on safety messaging or abandon the differentiated proposition.; If new evidence shows strong consumer demand for stylish hearing protection or high willingness to pay for certified products, the recommendation would be updated to prioritize a certified proposition.; If the test confirms that free entry-point provision significantly increases adoption, the recommendation would be to expand the pilot to multiple entry points rather than a single concert door.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Based on medical evidence linking excess body fat to heart disease, diabetes and certain cancers, Tanita introduced the world’s first integrated body composition analyzer/scale to the professional markets in 1992.
Tanita is a world leader in precision electronic scales. With almost 50% of its domestic market share, the name Tanita is a household name in Japan.
In Japan, every household has a bathroom scale (health meter), and most nowadays keep track of your body composition.

A body fat measuring apparatus for measuring body fat in a patient's body comprises apparatus for simultaneously measuring an impedance between the patient's feet, and for measuring the patient's height and the patient's weight

the impedance value of a body to be measured vary according to the date, time and differences of body condition before measurement. These various are too large to use the above-described inference formula accurately and amount of body fat calculated by the formula is likely to be inaccurate.
In 104 men and 101 women (16-78 years and BMI 16-41 kg/m2) the mean bias in body-fat mass measured using the Tanita body-fat analyser was 0.8 (2SD 7.9) kg relative to a four-compartment model.

This method is safe, noninvasive, provides rapid measurements, requires little operator skill and subject cooperation, and is portable. Further validation of this method is recommended in subjects with abnormal body composition.
These findings indicate the need for controlled measurement conditions to obtain valid body composition estimates using the TBI method in healthy people.
The Tanita TBF-310 foot-to-foot BIA body composition analyser with the manufacturer's prediction equations is not recommended for application to individual children who are overweight and obese

T1: Consumers will adopt a home body-fat scale if it provides a clear, actionable health message and is marketed as a personal wellness tool, because health awareness in the 1990s makes them willing to invest in devices that measure body fat for weight management. Who benefits: Individual consumers seeking to manage weight and improve health.. Why behaviour changes: Increased media coverage of health risks (heart disease, diabetes) and the availability of portable devices make consumers view body fat as a measurable health metric, prompting purchase for personal use.. How value is captured: Tanita would capture value through premium pricing for a differentiated consumer product and potential recurring revenue from accessories or subscription services for health tracking.. Assumptions: Consumers in 1993 are motivated by health concerns and are willing to pay for devices that provide measurable outcomes.; Marketing can effectively communicate the health benefits of body fat measurement to home users.; The technology can be adapted to a consumer-friendly form factor without compromising accuracy.. Predictions: A survey of target consumers would show at least 30% indicating intent to purchase a home body-fat scale for weight management.; Sales of a consumer version would exceed 5,000 units within the first year in a key market (e.g., Japan or the US)..

T2: Consumers will adopt a home body-fat scale if it is marketed as a medical-grade tool for professional use, because clinics and health clubs already use Tanita equipment and trust the brand, creating a perceived credibility that transfers to home users. Who benefits: Professional healthcare providers and clinics that need accurate body-fat measurements for patient care.. Why behaviour changes: Clinics and health clubs already purchase and rely on Tanita scales for clinical accuracy, so a consumer version would be seen as a compatible, trusted extension of that equipment, reducing perceived risk and increasing willingness to adopt. How value is captured: Tanita would capture value through higher-margin sales to professional channels and potential licensing of the technology to medical device manufacturers, leveraging existing brand credibility.. Assumptions: Professional users are willing to recommend a consumer version to colleagues.; The consumer version can meet the same accuracy standards expected in clinical settings.; Marketing can position the product as a professional-grade tool for home use.. Predictions: Professional users would indicate intent to purchase a consumer version at a rate at least 20% higher than a generic home scale.; Sales of a consumer version would be concentrated in clinics and health clubs, with fewer than 10% of units sold to individual consumers..

Test "Consumer vs Professional Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging. Recruit 500 participants (250 self-identified health-conscious adults and 250 professional users: clinics/health clubs). Randomly assign participants to one of two message groups: Group A receives a health-focused message about body fat measurement for weight management; Group B receives a professional-focused message about a trusted clinical tool for patient care. Both groups are shown a description of the same Tanita consumer body-fat scale and asked to indicate purchase intent on a 7-point scale (1‑10).. Sample: 500 participants (250 health-conscious adults and 250 professional users) recruited via online panels.. Measure: Purchase intent score (1‑10) for each message group.. Predictions: T1: Group A will have a purchase intent score at least 10 points higher than Group B.; T2: Group B will have a purchase intent score at least 10 points higher than Group A.. Decision rule: If Group A’s mean score is at least 10 points higher than Group B’s mean score, adopt T1. If Group B’s mean score is at least 10 points higher than Group A’s mean score, adopt T2. If the difference is less than 10 points, the test is inconclusive and further evidence is needed.. Cost: 8000 euros, 4 weeks.

Sample: 500 adults aged 18‑95 in the United States, recruited via an online panel, stratified by gender and income to ensure representation.. Predictions: T1: Higher purchase intent in the Health Monitoring condition compared to the Fitness Tracking condition.; T2: Higher purchase intent in the Fitness Tracking condition compared to the Health Monitoring condition.. Test "Free vs Fashion Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging condition. Participants view a product description of Hellberg's hearing protection (EN 352 certified, comfortable, safe). In Condition A, the description emphasizes free provision at events and free availability. In Condition B, the description emphasizes fashion and lifestyle appeal, positioning the product as a stylish accessory suitable for various activities. Participants are then asked to indicate purchase intent (1-7 scale) and whether they would purchase at a price point of €30.. Sample: 300 adult consumers aged 18-45, recruited via an online panel, balanced for gender and geographic region.. Measure: Purchase intent score (1-7) and willingness to pay (EUR).. T1: Homeowners will purchase a differentiated consumer lawn tractor because it becomes an affordable, convenient chore solution for small gardens and outdoor tasks, and Deere can capture value through premium pricing and brand differentiation. Who benefits: Individual homeowners with small gardens who previously lacked efficient outdoor equipment.. Why behaviour changes: Increased awareness of the convenience and practicality of garden tractors, combined with the desire for easier outdoor maintenance, makes ownership seem like a sensible purchase.. How value is captured: Deere can charge a premium price for a purpose-built consumer model, sell through independent dealers, and maintain brand prestige while capturing higher margins than standard farm equipment.. T2: Small‑farm owners will adopt a differentiated consumer lawn tractor because it reduces labor costs and improves efficiency for light‑to‑moderate farming tasks, and Deere can capture value through volume sales and service contracts. Why behaviour changes: Economic pressure to lower labor costs and the need for efficient equipment for light‑to‑moderate farming tasks makes a consumer‑grade lawn tractor seem like a cost‑effective investment.. How value is captured: Deere can sell through independent dealers, offer service and parts contracts, and capture volume sales while maintaining a premium price for a purpose‑built model.. Test "Consumer vs Small-Farm Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups: Group A receives a consumer-focused message emphasizing convenience, affordability, and ease of use for small gardens; Group B receives a small-farm-focused message emphasizing labor cost savings, efficiency, and suitability for light-to-moderate farming tasks. Both groups view a generic farm tractor model and are asked to indicate purchase intent on a 7-point scale (1‑10).. Sample: 300 participants: 150 homeowners with small gardens and 150 small-farm owners. Recruited via an online panel to ensure demographic representation.. Measure: Purchase intent score (1‑10) for the assigned message.. Predictions: T1: Group A will have a higher average purchase intent score than Group B.; T2: Group B will have a higher average purchase intent score than Group A.. Decision rule: If the difference in average scores between the two groups is at least 0.5 points (e.g., Group A’s score is at least 5.5 and Group B’s score is at least 4.5), conclude the theory with the higher score is supported. If the difference is less than 0.5, both theories remain plausible and further testing is needed.. Cost: 2000 euros, 4 weeks.

Test "Consumer vs Small-Farm Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups: Group A receives a consumer-focused message emphasizing a single, convenient tool for small-scale landscaping and gardening. Group B receives a small-farm owner-focused message emphasizing a versatile tool for multiple tasks. Both groups are shown a product description of a differentiated lawn tractor (e.g., Deere 4010) and asked to indicate purchase intent on a 7-point scale (1‑10).. Sample: 300 participants: 150 homeowners (small gardens) and 150 small-farm owners (hobby farmers). Recruited via an online panel to ensure demographic representation.. Measure: Purchase intent score (1‑10) for each group.. Predictions: T1: Group A will have a higher average purchase intent score than Group B.; T2: Group B will have a higher average purchase intent score than Group A.. Decision rule: If the average purchase intent score for Group A is at least 2 points higher than Group B, proceed with a differentiated consumer proposition targeting homeowners. If Group B’s score is at least 2 points higher, proceed with a differentiated small-farm proposition. If the difference is less than 2 points, do not commit to either proposition and conduct further market research.. Cost: 2000 euros, 4 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition targeting homeowners with small gardens, leveraging the existing tractor engineering to create a single, convenient tool for landscaping and gardening. This aligns with the observed rise in lawn and garden equipment sales and the popularity of the 4010 model. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition targeting homeowners with small gardens, leveraging the existing tractor engineering to create a single, convenient tool for landscaping and gardening. Target customer: Individual homeowners with small gardens who need a single tool for mowing, weeding, and light landscaping.. Value proposition: A differentiated lawn tractor that combines the durability and performance of a Deere tractor with a user-friendly design, offering a convenient, all-in-one solution for small-scale landscaping tasks.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed Consumer vs Small-Farm Messaging Test to validate purchase intent differences and decide whether to proceed with a consumer-focused launch.. Uncertainty: The willingness of homeowners to pay a premium for a differentiated lawn tractor is uncertain. Additionally, the competitive landscape and the size of the small-garden market in 1962 are not fully established.. Would change if: If the test shows that small-farm owners have a significantly higher purchase intent than homeowners, we would shift focus to a small-farm proposition.; If the test shows no meaningful difference in purchase intent between the two groups, we would recommend further market research before committing to either proposition.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Participants are recruited from home-studio creators and individual content creators.
